c.tagline: Diamond capital of Rubens, fashion, and Flemish grandeur.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis run on the meter with a rooftop sign; they are usually booked by app or taken from ranks at Central Station and squares rather than hailed on the street.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU emergency number for ambulance and fire; 101 reaches the police directly.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Het Eilandje: MAS Museum aan de Stroom Antwerp

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets around Central Station and De Coninckplein, which get seedy late at night.

hood_desc: The medieval core around the Grote Markt guild houses, the Cathedral of Our Lady, and the Rubenshuis; best for first-timers who want the landmarks, cobbled streets, and cafes all within a short walk.
The stylish southern district of grand avenues, the KMSKA and FoMu museums, galleries, and a dense strip of bars and restaurants; suits travellers after dining and nightlife with an arty edge.
The revitalised old-docklands quarter on the river, anchored by the striking MAS museum, marinas, warehouse lofts, and waterfront eateries; good for a trendy, up-and-coming base.
The fashion quarter around Nationalestraat and the MoMu fashion museum, lined with the boutiques of the 'Antwerp Six' and independent designers; a paradise for shoppers and style-seekers.
The bustling area around the cathedral-like Antwerpen-Centraal station, taking in the diamond district and a compact Chinatown; a convenient, well-connected base for arriving by train.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.pay: De Lijn tickets are cheapest bought before boarding via the app, machines, or shops (about €2.50 a ride); contactless bank cards also work when tapping on board. A day pass is around €7.50. Several central tram lines run underground as a 'premetro'.
transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5:30am to midnight; night service is limited to a few weekend lines, with taxis and ride apps filling the late gap.
transit.note: Antwerp has no full metro, but its tram network dives underground as a 'premetro' through the city centre.

transit.m: Train from Brussels Airport (BRU) to Antwerpen-Centraal, ~35-45 min

tip.r: Service is included in the bill; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service is appreciated but not expected.
